name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district lean (D+6 PVI) plus favorable environment
Incumbent Bill Keating running with a large cash advantage
Polymarket prices Keating at 96% to win
model.rationale: Keating combines incumbency, a big fundraising edge, and a district that leans Democratic in a strong Democratic environment, and markets price his win at 96 percent. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 19 points stands.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a much tighter race, or a late surge in Republican outside spending, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Keating, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by about six points. He has raised over $420,000 and holds nearly half a million dollars on hand, while Republican Tyler MacAllister has raised less and has only about $35,000 available. No outside groups are active in the race and no general-election polls have been published.

Prediction markets give Keating roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, and the fundamentals point to a comfortable margin near 19 points. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific evidence of a competitive contest.
